title: DNA Extraction and Multiplex PCR Genotyping of Brown Trout Microsatellites
author: Jarmo Koskiniemi
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bp7ymrpw
materials: DNA is extracted from dried scales or from fins or other tissues preserved in alcohol, frozen or fresh, or from eggs. The extractions are done using Qiagen DNeasy or DNAeasy 96 Blood & Tissue Kits with the kit manual’s ‘Animal Tissues’ protocols with a few modifications for the egg samples.

The PCRs are done using Qiagen Type-it Microsatellite Kit. The kit manual’s ‘Optimized cycling protocol for multiplex PCR amplification of microsatellites’ is used with the annealing temperature of 56°C, but with modifications on the reaction volumes. When the samples are fresh, or have been kept frozen or in alcohol for max. 1 year, 10 ul reactions are used. For max. 1 year old dried scales, 15 ul reactions are used. If samples are kept frozen or in alcohol for more than 1 year or if the dried scales are older than 1 year, 25 ul reactions are used. The extracted DNA is usually used without dilution. When the samples are very old, the extracted DNA is concentrated to 1/10 of the original volume by keeping the DNA in open tubes at room temperature. For the 10 ul reaction, 5 ul of kit's master mix and 3 ul of extracted DNA are used. For the 15 ul reaction, these volumes are multiplied by 1.5, and for 25 ul reactions by 2.5.

steps.title: Prepare Tissue Samples
steps.instruction: Prepare the appropriate biological sample for DNA extraction based on the source material.

substeps.instruction: For scales: Use 1 scale, or 2-3 scales if the fish are very small.
For other tissues: Cut a small piece (maximum 10 mg).
For samples stored in alcohol: Keep pieces in open tubes overnight to allow the alcohol to evaporate.

steps.title: Prepare Egg Samples
steps.instruction: Process eggs for DNA extraction using modified buffer volumes.

substeps.instruction: Puncture the eggs with sharp tweezers.
Increase the volume of the ATL-buffer and proteinase K mixture to be at least 4 times the volume of the egg.
Increase the volume of the AL-buffer and alcohol mixture to be 2.05 times the volume of the ATL-buffer and proteinase K mixture.

steps.title: Perform Multiplex PCR Genotyping
steps.instruction: Analyze 16 microsatellite loci using two multiplex reactions with the specified primers and concentrations.

substeps.instruction: Use the following primer pairs and concentrations: BS131 (0.10 µM, VIC), OneU9 (0.06 µM, VIC), SSA197 (0.02 µM, NED), SSA289 (0.50 µM, PET), SSA407 (0.15 µM, NED), SSA85 (0.02 µM, VIC), SSOSL311 (0.15 µM, NED), SSOSL417 (0.08 µM, PET), SSOSL438 (0.15 µM, VIC), SSsp1605 (0.04 µM, NED), SSsp2201 (0.03 µM, 6FAM), Str15INRA (0.10 µM, 6FAM), Str60INRA (0.08 µM, PET), Str73INRA (0.08 µM, VIC), Str85INRA (0.60 µM, 6FAM), and Strutta58 (0.10 µM, 6FAM).

steps.title: Sequence and Analyze DNA
steps.instruction: Detect and analyze genotypes using automated sequencing equipment and software.

substeps.instruction: Sequence samples using an Applied Biosystems ABI 3130 automated DNA sequencer.
Use Applied Biosystems GeneScan 500LIZ as the size standard.
Analyze data using GeneMapper analysis software v5.0.
Manually check and correct automatic outputs for errors.
